title: All Cultures Are Local
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article distinguishes organization-wide culture from the day-to-day team 'climate' shaped almost entirely by an immediate manager, arguing that most people experience the latter far more than the former. Citing Gallup research that managers account for roughly 70% of the variance in team engagement, it makes the case that a single weak local leader can quietly erode a team's experience even while the broader organization's stated values remain unchanged. The piece offers concrete early warning signs of eroding team climate, like decisions moving to email chains or team members routing around their manager, and recommends frequent, team-specific pulse surveys to catch problems before they show up in annual results. It closes with the reminder that culture is ultimately built one team and one leader at a time, not declared from the top.

quotes: But the culture that team members actually experience is shaped most strongly by their immediate environment, not by the organization's corporate culture.

Culture is the stable, organization-wide set of values and norms that shape meaning and experience. Climate is the local weather system a team lives inside day to day, shaped almost entirely by its leader and colleagues.
Managers across the globe account for at least 70% of the variance in team engagement.
One weak leader who allows communication to become fragmented and relationships to become transactional can ruin the experience of everyone on the team.
Culture isn’t declared at the enterprise level. It is built one team, one leader, and one conversation at a time.
